q: Match the northern cru to a defining producer.
exp: Vernay saved Condrieu from extinction at ~8 ha in the 1960s.

q: Clairette de Die's ancestral-method sparkler ferments once from which aromatic majority grape?
ans: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (méthode ancestrale)
exp: The Tradition style is ≥75% Muscat; crémant de Die is Clairette-based.

q: Which IGP surrounds the northern Rhône and launched countless négociant Syrahs, its name meaning 'hills of the Rhône'?
exp: Where young growers park declassified or young-vine Syrah and Viognier.

q: Tavel's rosé tradition permits how many varieties, led by Grenache and Cinsault?
exp: Nine; Tavel remains France's only all-rosé cru.

q: Up to what percentage of Viognier may Côte-Rôtie co-ferment with its Syrah?
exp: Twenty percent is the legal ceiling, and it is rarely approached — most estates use none or a few percent, with Guigal's La Mouline the famous outlier at around 11%. The grapes are co-fermented, not blended afterwards: Viognier's phenolics help stabilise anthocyanins, so the wine actually gains colour while gaining apricot lift. Learn the northern trio as an asymmetry — Côte-Rôtie 20% white permitted, Hermitage 15%, Cornas none at all.

q: Hermitage rouge may legally include white grapes. Which, and up to how much?
accept: marsanne and roussanne up to fifteen percent
up to 15% marsanne roussanne co-fermented into the red
fifteen percent white grapes marsanne or roussanne permitted
marsanne roussanne maximum 15 percent though rarely used now
ans: Up to 15% Marsanne and/or Roussanne, co-fermented — though almost nobody exercises the right today
exp: The allowance is a relic of field-blend farming on the hill, when growers picked and pressed the parcel as it stood. It is now largely theoretical, because Hermitage Blanc is too valuable to bury in red. Hold it beside Côte-Rôtie's 20% Viognier, which is genuinely used, and Cornas's flat prohibition on white grapes, which is that appellation's whole identity.

q: Gigondas gained a new colour in 2023. Which, and on which grape does the decree rest?
accept: white wine with clairette at a minimum of 70 percent
gigondas blanc based on clairette at least seventy percent
a white appellation resting on clairette from the 2023 vintage
ans: White — Gigondas Blanc, built on Clairette at a minimum 70% of the blend, from the 2023 harvest
exp: This is a climate decision dressed as a legal one: Clairette holds acidity and stays comparatively low in alcohol in heat, which is why the southern Rhône is turning back to a grape it spent forty years grubbing up. Gigondas was promoted from Côtes du Rhône Villages to cru in 1971 for reds and rosés only; the white joins them from 2023, while the red still requires Grenache at its core.

q: Syrah's parentage was settled by DNA analysis in 1998. Name both parents and their home regions.
accept: dureza of the ardeche crossed with mondeuse blanche of savoie
mondeuse blanche and dureza both french alpine varieties
dureza from ardeche and mondeuse blanche from savoie are syrah's parents
ans: Dureza, an obscure red from the Ardèche, crossed with Mondeuse Blanche from the Savoie — a wholly French, wholly Rhône-Alpes origin
exp: The finding killed the romantic origin stories — Shiraz in Persia, Syracuse, a Crusader knight — and replaced them with two near-extinct locals from either side of the northern Rhône. It matters practically too: Mondeuse Noire is a half-sibling of Syrah, which is why a Savoie Mondeuse can flash black pepper and blue fruit and derail a blind flight.

q: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's minimum natural alcohol, the highest of any French appellation, is:
exp: 12.5%, written into Baron Le Roy's 1936 decree when ripeness was both a mark of quality and genuinely hard to reach in cool years. Today it is cleared by mid-September and the real struggle is holding wines under 15.5%. Pair it with the 35 hl/ha yield ceiling — among the lowest in France for an appellation of that size — and you have the two numbers that shape the cru's structure and its modern predicament.

q: Saint-Joseph is the northern Rhône's structural problem child. Explain what happened to its boundaries and why that matters to a buyer.
accept: expanded from six communes to twenty-six over about fifty kilometres
it grew from 6 to 26 communes and spread onto flat land so quality became uneven
1956 six villages then enlarged along the west bank and now being pulled back to slopes
over-extended appellation so the producer matters far more than the name
ans: Created in 1956 across six communes of granite slope, it was expanded to 26 communes running some 50 kilometres down the west bank, dragging the name onto flat alluvial ground it was never meant to cover; a delimitation review has since been pulling the appellation back toward the hillsides. The label alone therefore tells you almost nothing — you buy the grower and the lieu-dit
exp: This is why Saint-Joseph holds both the best values and the sharpest disappointments in the north. The historic core sits around Tournon, Mauves and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols — Trollat's old ground, now largely worked by Gonon and Chave. Learn those village names and the appellation becomes legible instead of a lottery.

q: Junmai Daiginjo requires what maximum seimaibuai?
ans: ≤50% remaining (half the grain polished away), no added alcohol
exp: Daiginjo with brewer's alcohol drops the 'Junmai'.

q: Yamahai and Kimoto methods differ from modern sokujō by:
accept: natural lactic starter no added lactic acid
wild lactic acid development slow moto
ans: Building the starter's lactic acidity naturally (kimoto with pole-mashing; yamahai without) instead of adding lactic acid
exp: Gamier, deeper, higher-acid styles — sake's 'natural wine' lineage.

accept: amylase converts rice starch to fermentable sugar
ans: Saccharification — Aspergillus oryzae's amylases convert rice starch to sugar as yeast ferments it (multiple parallel fermentation)
exp: Sake's defining trick; beer does the steps sequentially.

q: Name two premier sake rice varieties beyond Yamada Nishiki.
ans: e.g., Gohyakumangoku (clean, northern), Omachi (ancient, wilder), Miyama Nishiki
exp: Shinpaku — the starchy white heart — is what polishing exposes.
